written.myAnswer: Lipids commonly contain glycerol and fatty acids. Glycerol has the structure CH₂OH–CHOH–CH₂OH, and a fatty acid has a long hydrocarbon chain attached to a carboxyl group (R–COOH).

Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains with a carboxyl group (–COOH) at one end. Saturated fatty acids have no carbon–carbon double bonds and carry the maximum number of hydrogen atoms; they are generally solid at room temperature. Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon–carbon double bonds and are generally liquid at room temperature.

Fats and oils are made of one glycerol molecule joined to three fatty acids. Fats are generally rich in saturated fatty acids and are solid at room temperature, whereas oils are generally rich in unsaturated fatty acids and are liquid. Lipids stored in adipose tissue provide a long-term energy reserve; when needed, they are broken down and used as fuel.
